summary: This page is Snowflake's reference for the SHOW PACKAGES POLICIES command, which lists packages policy information. It covers the optional IN SCHEMA scope syntax, the output columns (created_on, name, database_name, schema_name, kind, owner, comment, owner_role_type), and the privileges required, which are OWNERSHIP or USAGE on the packages policy. Usage notes say the command needs no running warehouse and that LIMIT rows cannot exceed 10000.
one_line: Snowflake reference for the SHOW PACKAGES POLICIES command, covering its scope syntax, output columns, privileges, and row limit.
key_facts: The SHOW PACKAGES POLICIES command lists packages policy information.
The optional IN clause accepts SCHEMA, SCHEMA <schema_name>, or <schema_name> to set the command's scope.
If no database is in use, specifying SCHEMA has no effect on the output.
The output column created_on gives the date and time when the policy was created.
The output column owner_role_type is either ROLE or DATABASE_ROLE, and returns APPLICATION if a Snowflake Native App owns the object.
Snowflake returns NULL for owner_role_type if the object was deleted, because a deleted object does not have an owner role.
Running SHOW PACKAGES POLICIES requires OWNERSHIP or USAGE privilege on the packages policy.
OWNERSHIP is automatically granted to the role that created the object but can be transferred using the role with the MANAGE GRANTS privilege.
USAGE on a packages policy also grants the ability to execute a SHOW or DESCRIBE command on the packages policy.
Operating on any object in a schema also requires USAGE privilege on the parent database and schema.
The command does not require a running warehouse to execute.
The value for LIMIT rows cannot exceed 10000.
If LIMIT rows is omitted, the command results in an error when the result set is larger than 10K rows.
Results with more than 10K records can be viewed by including LIMIT rows or by querying the corresponding view in the Snowflake Information Schema.
The example statement is SHOW PACKAGES POLICIES;
